prompt: I just joined this team. Walk me through the codebase.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, ~400 TypeScript files, index never built.
rubric: Runs `graph-it scan` first
Runs `graph-it architecture --format toon` to get the workspace overview
Identifies entry points, business-logic core and the most complex module as separate steps
Ends with a critical-path trace rendered as `--format mermaid` for the human reader
Delivers the structured Project Tour report: 3 entry points table, business logic core table, most complex module, Mermaid critical path
anti_patterns: Summarises the repository from file names without running graph-it commands
Uses mermaid for the intermediate agent-facing steps instead of toon
gold_notes: Six-step workflow: scan, architecture, entry points, business logic, complexity, trace.

prompt: What are the entry points of this project?
context: Repo root: /work/shop. Candidates by name: src/index.ts, src/cli.ts, src/server.ts, src/app.ts, src/core/registry.ts.
rubric: Runs both directions per candidate: `graph-it explain <file>` (outgoing) and `find_referencing_files --targetPath=<abs>` (incoming)
Ranks true entry points as high fan-out with zero fan-in
Classifies a high fan-in, many-exports file as shared core rather than an entry point
Limits the candidate sweep (max ~5) and selects the top 3
Describes each selected entry point with its role, callers and top downstream modules
anti_patterns: Declares entry points from filename conventions alone
gold_notes: Ranking rules 1-4 in step 3 of the skill.

prompt: Where does the actual business logic live in this repo?
context: Repo root: /work/shop with src/services, src/domain, src/handlers, src/utils.
rubric: Runs `generate_codemap --filePath=<abs>` for the outgoing view of each candidate
Runs `find_referencing_files --targetPath=<abs>` for the incoming view
Selects the 1-3 files scoring highest on both exported-symbol count and fan-in
Explains the discriminants: rich exports with no importers is dead code; many importers with few exports is a utility hub
Uses absolute paths for the tool calls
anti_patterns: Picks folders by name without measuring fan-in and exports
Runs only one of the two directions
gold_notes: Business logic sits at the intersection of many exports and many importers.

prompt: Which module is the most complex and risky to touch?
rubric: Runs `graph-it tool analyze_file_logic --filePath=<abs>` on a representative sample (top ~20 by size, or all files under 50)
Scores with the documented heuristic: call depth and internal cycles weighted high; exports, fan-in and fan-out medium
Names the highest-scoring file and gives its concrete signals
States that the heuristic is architectural, not cyclomatic, and suggests pairing with a linter for line-level complexity
Recommends get_impact_analysis before modifying the high-blast-radius file
anti_patterns: Uses line count as the complexity measure
Presents the natural-language query answer as the verified result
gold_notes: graph-it query is a hypothesis generator; deterministic scores confirm it.

prompt: Show me the main execution path end to end, with a diagram I can put in the onboarding doc.
context: Repo root: /work/shop, top entry point src/index.ts, main function `main`.
rubric: Runs `graph-it trace src/index.ts#main --format mermaid`
Justifies mermaid because the output is rendered for a human in Markdown
Notes that toon remains the default for the other steps of the tour
Embeds the trace output in the Critical Path section of the Project Tour report
anti_patterns: Uses `--format mermaid` for outputs the agent has to parse
Hand-draws a diagram instead of using the trace output
gold_notes: mermaid renders in VS Code, GitHub and Obsidian previews.

prompt: The architecture command returns way too much data on this repo.
context: Repo root: /work/platform monorepo, packages/api, packages/web, packages/shared, ~4000 files.
rubric: Restricts the pass with `graph-it architecture --maxFiles 300 --format toon`
Recommends touring one package at a time: `cd packages/api && graph-it scan`, then repeat the workflow
Reports the unanalysed area explicitly instead of guessing about it
Re-runs `graph-it scan` from the package root when indexing is incomplete
anti_patterns: Guesses at the structure of the unindexed area
Keeps the full-graph request and truncates the output by hand
gold_notes: Monorepo tip: scope the tour per package; lower --maxFiles.
